title: Bilge Corrosion Protection and Frame Foot Renewal in the Aft Belly Fairing Area, Section 15
abstract: Permanent treatment of the standing water problem below the aft cabin on early-build twin-engine aircraft, combining a renewed frame foot with an interrupted seal, a re-cut water escape route and a sprayed inhibitor over the whole bilge.

sections.reason: Twelve operators of pre-2011 twin-engine aircraft now report the same condition at heavy check: water standing on the skin between the frame feet below the aft cabin, wet insulation, and pitting or exfoliation at the frame foot itself. Across a sampled population of 148 aircraft above 50 000 flight hours, 96 showed material loss somewhere between frame 55 and frame 66 and 21 were beyond the limits of the applicable repair scheme. The finding is not new, but the rate is rising as the fleet ages and as operators keep aircraft in service past the original design service goal. Two operators have written to say that the unscheduled structural content in this area is now the single biggest source of heavy check overrun on the type, and one has put a figure of 71 aircraft-days over three years on it. The existing answer, which is to clean, treat and re-inspect, does not stop the water arriving.
sections.description: The change treats the cause and the consequence together. The frame feet between frame 55 and frame 66 are renewed with an interrupted faying seal so that water reaching the foot can escape into the stringer 44 escape route rather than sitting behind it; the seal is broken over a 15 mm land at the lowest point of each foot, which is the figure the design office arrived at from the bilge geometry. The lower frame cleat assembly D5331118141717 and the outboard shear tie sub-assembly D5331119974905 are re-issued with the seal land machined in and the forward frame doubler RO920514-03 is added where material has already been lost. A local skin doubler kit D5331120068647 is installed at the two lowest stringer penetrations, which is where the escape route is re-cut. The joint is closed with tension head bolts AGS713311K3, shear head bolts EN505957-8B and plain washers AGS334024-84. The whole bilge between the two frames is then washed, dried and sprayed with a water-displacing inhibitor to the standard practice for surface treatment. The aft cargo wiring ground stud position 551VC and the landing gear bay backshell position 3061VC both sit in the sprayed area and have to be masked and re-terminated. Access is from inside the aft cargo compartment in zones 133 and 142 and from the aft belly fairing in zones 191 and 192. Detail is on drawings D53311127475 and D53311186914.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 12.6 kg per aircraft, symmetric, with a centre-of-gravity shift below 0.04 per cent MAC. No electrical load change, although two ground points are disturbed and must be bonded and tested after the inhibitor is applied. The renewed frame foot is not interchangeable with the original because the seal land and the fastener pattern change together. The intended benefit is that the corrosion inspection of this bilge moves from a 4C to an 8C interval and that the unscheduled repair content disappears; the revised interval depends on a fresh corrosion susceptibility assessment which is not yet complete. AMM zonal, cleaning and drainage content for ATA 53-31 requires update, the aft cargo wiring sheet requires a revised ground point note, and at least one existing repair scheme in this bay will have to be re-issued.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Provisional estimate is nine days inside a scheduled 12-year check on the assumption that the aft cargo compartment and the belly fairing are already open for other work. No production cut-in is proposed: the affected build standard is no longer produced.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm whether the sprayed inhibitor is compatible with the equipment already installed in the aft belly fairing, whether the existing bilge repair scheme survives the frame foot renewal, and whether the modification can be embodied on aircraft that have not had the chromate-free protection and drainage standard applied at the forward cargo door surround.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation, CG shift below 0.04 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in proposed; the affected build standard is out of production
